old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a steaming hot pot filled with a variety of ingredients, including mushrooms, enoki mushrooms, leafy greens, and possibly tofu or other vegetables. The hot pot is divided into two sections, each containing different types of food. Steam rises from the pot, indicating it is freshly cooked and ready to be eaten. In the background, there are white cups on the table, suggesting a dining setting. Skewers with food items are lowered into the pot. The scene is set in what appears to be a casual dining environment, with the focus primarily on the hot pot and the act of lowering food on skewers into it. The video emphasizes the communal and interactive nature of the meal, highlighting the shared experience of enjoying food together.

The hot pot is divided into two sections, each containing different types of food. Steam rises from the pot, indicating it is freshly cooked and ready to be eaten. In the background, there are white cups on the table, suggesting a dining setting. A person's hand appears in the frame, holding chopsticks and placing food into the pot. The hand moves methodically, adding pieces of food into the broth, which is bubbling gently. The scene is set in what appears to be a casual dining environment, with the focus primarily on the hot pot and the act of cooking and eating. The video emphasizes the communal and interactive nature of the meal, highlighting the shared experience of preparing and enjoying food together.
caption: The video captures a close, eye-level view of a two-compartment metal hot pot filled with dark simmering broth and an assortment of ingredients, including shiitake, oyster and enoki mushrooms, bean sprouts, and green leafy vegetables. A white cup sits on the left and a white plate on the right, with a person in pink and black clothing behind the pot. A bamboo skewer threaded with puffed fried-tofu pieces and a red-and-white crab stick moves downward from the top edge of the frame into the left compartment. The skewered items settle at the rim, the wooden sticks protruding upward as they rest just inside the broth. Wisps of steam grow more visible, drifting upward over the left compartment as the segment progresses. The pot, its contents, and the background objects remain fixed in position, with no clear camera pan or zoom. The descent of the skewer is object motion rather than a change in viewpoint. The broth continues to simmer beneath the resting skewered pieces, steam rising steadily from the surface.

without inventing how it began or how it ultimately ends. A process may already be happening
on the first frame and still be happening after the last. Do not force the endpoints to match,
infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
